If the rate is Above 0.541 at that time, the market resolves to Yes. If not, the market resolves to No. 
Revisions to the underlying made after expiration will not be accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.
Rounding to four decimal places shall be assumed unless otherwise specified.
If no data is available from Pyth at the specified time, the most recently available value will be used.

markets.rules_secondary:
Source Agency: The Source Agencies are, in hierarchical order, S&P Dow Jones Indices, a division of S&P Global, the Pyth Network, including the values of the S&P 500 published through its official price feeds, Bloomberg, the Wall Street Journal, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, and CNBC.

Where the specified time period does not specify a time of day, the value of the S&P 500 during the specified time period is its official closing value for each trading day falling within the specified time period. The official closing value of the S&P 500 for a trading day is the final daily index level designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices as the official close for that trading day, as published by the Source Agencies, measured to two (2) decimal places. Intraday values, opening values, daily highs or lows, and pre-market or after-hours indicative values are not the official closing value and are not accounted for in determining the Expiration Value in that case.

The value of the S&P 500 refers only to the level of the S&P 500 index as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices. Prices published by the Pyth Network or any other Source Agency for exchange-traded products tracking the S&P 500, S&P 500 futures, options, or perpetual contracts, or the constituent stocks of the S&P 500 are not the value of the S&P 500 and are not accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.

Only trading days for which S&P Dow Jones Indices calculates an official closing value of the S&P 500 are taken into account in determining whether the Payout Criterion is satisfied during the specified time period. Weekends and days on which the U.S. equity markets are closed are not trading days and are disregarded. Trading days are determined by reference to Eastern Time.

Where the close value or time is specified, if trading on any trading day falling within the specified time period is conducted as an abbreviated session (including a scheduled early close) or is halted before the scheduled close (including due to a market-wide circuit breaker), the official closing value designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices for that trading day governs.

Changes to the constituents, weightings, or divisor of the S&P 500, and changes to its published methodology, do not affect the Contract; the value as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices and published by the Source Agencies governs.

If the S&P 500 is renamed, rebranded, or reidentified, its ticker symbol or index code is changed, or the business unit calculating or publishing it is reorganized or renamed but its value continues to be calculated and published under the same or a successor name or identifier reflecting the continuation of the S&P 500 record, that continued record governs and the Contract remains open. If the S&P 500 is discontinued and no successor continues its record, the no-data clarification below governs.

If the Source Agencies conflict as to the value of the S&P 500, the hierarchy set out in Source Agency above will govern. Continuing ambiguity or dispute will be resolved by Kalshi pursuant to Rule 7.1.

If there is no data for the Underlying published by any Source Agency by the Expiration Date, all markets will resolve to No, unless a “No data” strike is listed, in which case the “No data” strike will resolve Yes and all others will resolve No. For the avoidance of doubt, if the U.S. equity markets are unexpectedly closed on every day falling within the specified time period, such that no official value of the S&P 500 is calculated for any trading day falling within the specified time period, this clarification governs.

If a Source Agency corrects, revises, or retracts a value of the S&P 500 prior to Expiration, the corrected value governs; corrections published after Expiration are not accounted for. If the Exchange determines that a published value of the S&P 500 contains a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published, and if none is published by the Expiration Date, the no-data clarification above governs.
